h2: MFL tank floor scanning in Tampa: terminal tank farms, sulfur storage and API 653 floor data
html:
MFL tank floor scanning in Tampa: terminal tank farms, sulfur storage and API 653 floor data

In Tampa, MFL is used mainly to scan the floors of aboveground storage tanks at the fuel terminals on Port Tampa Bay, which handle nearly half of Florida's petroleum supply. Each scan happens when the tank is out of service, cleaned and open for its API 653 internal inspection. Indications are then sized by ultrasonic prove-up. Atlantis is Houston-based and sends scanning crews to the site.

The tank population. Florida has no refineries, so the tanks around the bay hold imported product for distribution. Kinder Morgan's main Tampa terminal has 31 tanks of 9,500 to 120,000 barrels. They hold:

  • gasoline blendstock and premium gasoline;
  • ultra-low sulfur diesel;
  • jet fuel;
  • ethanol and biodiesel.

Buckeye, Global Partners, Chevron and Citgo run further terminals nearby. Floor problems depend on the product and the foundation. On the product side, water collecting in the tank bottom can lead to pitting and microbial corrosion. On the soil side, corrosion develops wherever the cathodic protection or the pad drainage has fallen behind.

What a floor scan delivers. An MFL scanner covers the main floor plate quickly and flags metal loss on the top and the underside of the plate for UT follow-up. Scanners cannot work right up against the shell, so the critical zone next to the shell and the annular ring are finished with hand UT. The deliverable is a floor map with the remaining thickness at each confirmed indication. The owner's API 653 inspector uses it to set the next internal interval and to decide between repairs, patch plates and a new bottom. Atlantis supplies the scan, the prove-up and the data, and it does not act as the API 653 inspector of record.

Getting usable data from one entry. Floor results depend on how well the tank was prepared. Product, sludge and scale left on the plate reduce sensitivity. Lap welds, patch plates and sumps leave areas the scanner cannot cover, and those areas are marked on the map rather than reported as clean. When a tank has had a coated bottom or a second bottom installed, tell the crew before mobilization, because both change the scanner setup and what the readings mean.

Sulfur and process tanks. Outside the fuel terminals, Mosaic's Riverview plant stores and handles molten sulfur for its three sulfuric acid plants. A heated tank of that kind is costly to empty and clean, so a single entry has to answer as much as possible. Scope the MFL floor scan, the UT prove-up and the shell thickness readings together. That way the owner does not have to open the tank again for data that was missed.

Timing in Tampa. A terminal tank out of service has to be covered by other tanks in the same product while fuel keeps moving inland by pipeline and truck. Book the scanning crew for the date the tank will be clean and gas-free, not for the start of the outage, to avoid standby time. Leave slack in the plan for the June to November hurricane season. In October 2024, Kinder Morgan shut its Tampa terminals ahead of Hurricane Milton.

Next steps. MFL tank floor inspection explains the method and the report. Aboveground storage tank inspection covers the full tank scope. API 653 tank NDE support sets out what Atlantis does, and does not do, within the owner's program. Tank inspection in Tampa is the local page. Send the tank list and outage dates.
